newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-WARNE AND BEVAN SPIN S.AFRICA TO DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WARNE AND BEVAN SPIN S.AFRICA TO DEFEAT.

text.p: Shane Warne and Michael Bevan hurried Australia to victory over South Africa by an innings and 196 runs with irresistible wrist spin bowling on the final morning of the first test on Tuesday.
South Africa, 302 behind on first innings, collapsed from their overnight 99 for four to 130 all out in just over an hour, losing the last five wickets for three runs in five overs.
Warne removed the remaining specialist batsmen, Jacques Kallis and Jonty Rhodes, to finish with four for 43 and Bevan polished off the rest of the innings to end with four for 32.
It was the first time South Africa had lost by an innings in 33 years, stretching back to 1964-65 when England won the first test in Durban by an innings and 104 runs.
Australian captain Mark Taylor said he was not really surprised South Africa collapsed so quickly.
"I wouldn't fancy it if I had to bat a day against Shane Warne and he's got 250 runs behind him," Taylor said.
"Shane is pretty close to being back to his best right now. He got six wickets in this game, all top order players and we had the luxury of Michael Bevan to knock over the tail."
Taylor described the result as a very satisfying victory.

"Of all the tests I've played in this one ranks right up there. Three years ago we played a very ordinary test here, we lost and had two players fined (Warne and Merv Hughes, but this is an emphatic vctory and we're absolutely delighted."
Taylor was almost blase about the batting of Steve Waugh, who was joint man of the match with Greg Blewett. "That's just a regulation innings from Steve if you look at the last three years.

"If you look back at the stand you'd probably pick out Greg's shots as the highlights, but Steve's value is that he never gives you a chance. He comes off after scoring 160 and he's genuinely disappointed at getting out."

South African captain Hansie Cronje said: "We just weren't on the same ballpark and we were completely outplayed. We will have to raise the standard of our batting, bowling and even fielding by at least 200 percent."
When fifth wicket pair Kallis and Rhodes resumed at the start of the day, they held firm for 10 overs until Rhodes was trapped lbw by Warne for eight.
Shaun Pollock and Kallis were together for a further six overs before Warne bowled Kallis round his legs for the innings top score of 39, and from that point the writing was on the wall.
Bevan wrapped up the lower order with his left-arm spin, snapping up the last four wickets for two runs in his last two overs.

Lance Klusener (0) and Dave Richardson (2) were caught by Matthew Hayden at short leg off the first and sixth balls of Bevan's 14th over, and Allan Donald and Paul Adams were both bowled without scoring in his 15th.
The second test in the three-match series starts in Port Elizabeth on March 14.
